findings.evidence: The submit-stack example takes `$ARGUMENTS` as the basis for the commit message, then shows `git commit -m "[Single sentence summary of what was done]"`. Double-quoted shell text still expands dollar expressions and command substitutions, contradicting SKILL.md's required single-quoted encoding for argument-derived values.
findings.fix: Add an explicit encoding step for the final commit message: encode it as one single-quoted shell word, escaping embedded single quotes, then run `git commit -m <encoded-message>`. Update the example snippet accordingly and preserve its upstream attribution.

findings.evidence: The checklist requires an approved update to have 'no other skill or command shares the name (if one does, stop and use the step 2 template)'. When both a same-named skill and command exist, as in the collision fixture, approving either offered update returns to the same collision menu rather than completing the update.
findings.fix: Make the initial collision offer distinguish viable resolutions: a renamed command, an explicitly approved resolution of the shadowing collision before updating the command, or routing a requested SKILL.md edit out of scope. Carry the selected resolution into the approved-update checklist instead of returning to the unchanged menu.

findings.evidence: 'The frontmatter is read only when `---` is on line 1; broken YAML loads the body with no fields and no error' repeats the same loading constraint stated again in Gotchas at line 92.
findings.fix: Keep the complete silent-frontmatter warning and its auto-invocation consequence once in Gotchas; replace the repeated explanation in Frontmatter with a short cross-reference.
